content.text:
View A represents a green triangle at the upper location as the dominant, currently selected item and the most accessible object. The left location holds a red, mostly square item with low immediate availability; the lower location holds a blue cross with modest but lower access; the right location holds a yellow circle with very low access. Recoverability for all items decays with additional steps, with the upper item remaining the best retrievable. Commands in A reliably move selection to the targeted location, so attention can be redirected to any of the four positions and the system will nearly always allocate to the commanded spot (high controllability).

View B represents a blue circle at upper, a red square at right, a yellow triangle at lower, and a green cross at left. The left green cross is the current focus and is the most accessible now; the lower yellow triangle and upper blue circle are moderately accessible; the right red square is least accessible. Recoverability for all declines over successive steps. Commands in B mostly drive selection to the upper location regardless of the commanded target, so this view is poorly controllable: attempts to redirect attention tend to land on the upper item.
